Drift of a whole table between two releases

Source: R/drtab.R
drfttab.Rd

Compares a reference table and a current one column by column, with the tests of this family: a numeric (or date) column by the two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test (drftks()) and the population stability index (drftpsi()), a text, factor or logical column by the chi-square test of homogeneity (drfthomog()). drftcal() then says how often these screens fire on a table that has not changed at all, which is what a flag has to be read against.

Usage

drfttab(
  ref,
  cur,
  alpha = 0.01,
  psithr = 0.25,
  psiminn = 100L,
  bins = 10L,
  seed = 1L
)

drftcal(
  data,
  n = 50L,
  alpha = 0.01,
  seed = 1L,
  psithr = 0.25,
  psiminn = 100L,
  bins = 10L
)

Arguments

ref, cur

The reference and the current table: data frames. Only the columns named in both are compared.

alpha

The level of each column's test, in (0, 1).

psithr

The population stability index above which a numeric column is flagged; 0.25 is the conventional "material shift".

psiminn

The fewest values each sample needs for psithr to count.

bins

The number of quantile bins of the reference, one whole number from 2 to 1,000,000; fewer are used when quantiles tie.

seed

The seed of the Monte Carlo p-value drfthomog() uses for small expected counts, and in drftcal() of the random splits too (there a whole number from 0: cunif() draws a seed for each split from it, and a split takes the rows of the smaller half of the uniforms drawn at its seed, so a seed gives the same splits in every language of the package).

data

One table, known not to have drifted (one release).

n

The number of random half-splits, from 1 to 1,000,000.

Value

drfttab() an object of class drfttab, a data frame with a row per shared column: column, type ("numeric" or "label"), test, statistic, p, psi (NA for a label column), nref, ncur, flag and note; the attributes only (the columns in one table alone), alpha, psithr and psiminn. drftcal() an object of class drftcal, a list: columns, a data frame of column and far (the share of splits on which it was flagged); anyflag, the share of splits with at least one flag; alpha; n; and alphafam, alpha divided by the number of columns, the level per column that holds the chance of any false flag at alpha (Bonferroni).

Details

drfttab() screens the columns the two tables share. A column is flagged when its test rejects at alpha, or when its population stability index is above psithr and both samples have at least psiminn values (on fewer, binning noise alone crosses the usual bands). A column that cannot be tested (all missing on one side, one category, of a type that is neither numbers nor labels) has flag NA, and note says why. Missing values are left out of each test; nref and ncur are the counts that entered it.

Many columns mean many tests: at alpha 0.01, one column in a hundred is flagged on unchanged data by the tests alone. drftcal() measures this for the table at hand: it splits data at random into two halves n times, runs drfttab() on each pair, and reports the share of splits on which each column, and any column, was flagged. Each half has half the rows, so the rates describe a comparison at that size.

Both functions exist in every language of the package. One branch is R's alone: a column of labels with an expected count below 5 gets its p-value from a Monte Carlo draw of R's generator (drfthomog()); the other languages leave such a column untested (flag missing) and say so in note.

Errors: ref, cur or data not a data frame; no shared column; alpha outside (0, 1); psithr not a positive number; psiminn, bins or n not a whole number of at least 1 (bins at least 2, n at most 1,000,000); fewer than four rows in data; a seed that is not one whole number (drftcal(): from 0).

References

Dunn, O. J. (1961). Multiple comparisons among means. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 56(293), 52-64. doi:10.1080/01621459.1961.10482090

Massey, F. J. (1951). The Kolmogorov-Smirnov test for goodness of fit. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 46(253), 68-78. doi:10.1080/01621459.1951.10500769

Wu, D. and Olson, D. L. (2010). Enterprise risk management: coping with model risk in a large bank. Journal of the Operational Research Society, 61(2), 179-190. doi:10.1057/jors.2008.144

See also

drftks(), drftpsi(), drfthomog() for one column.

Examples

set.seed(1)
ref <- data.frame(age = rnorm(300, 35, 9),
                  charge = sample(c("assault", "theft", "drugs"), 300, TRUE))
cur <- data.frame(age = rnorm(300, 39, 9),
                  charge = sample(c("assault", "theft", "drugs"), 300, TRUE))
drfttab(ref, cur)
#> drfttab: 2 columns, 1 flagged, 0 not testable (alpha 0.01, PSI above 0.25)
#>  column    type        test statistic        p   psi nref ncur  flag
#>     age numeric          ks     0.200 1.23e-05 0.309  300  300  TRUE
#>  charge   label homogeneity     2.029 3.63e-01    NA  300  300 FALSE
# how often the screens fire when nothing changed
drftcal(ref, n = 20)
#> drftcal: 20 half-splits of unchanged data at alpha 0.01
#> any column flagged on 5% of splits; per-column level for a family-wise 0.01: 0.005
#>  column  far
#>  charge 0.05
try(drfttab(ref, data.frame(other = 1)))
#> Error : drfttab: `ref` and `cur` share no column.
